A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StFT/StFT-F research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on plasma MHD, Navier-Stokes, and shallow-water systems, including quantitative comparisons, uncertainty visualizations, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds DPOT comparisons, tokenizer and scale-count ablations, computational measurements, and uncertainty-coverage results.

M1.justification: The coarse-to-fine hierarchy, dual processing paths, overlapping tokenization, summed block predictions, and rectified-flow residual correction are retained. Splitting Algorithm 1 into two algorithms and clarifying conditioning do not establish a changed procedure; v1 already documented time conditioning in Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three physical systems with the same domains, variables, and data-generation conditions in Appendix A. The added ablations, profiling, and coverage measurements use retained datasets. PDEBench appears as baseline provenance, not as an additional evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: v2 adds AR-DPOT, described as an AFNO variant, to Table 1 and trajectory comparisons across all three systems. It becomes the strongest external comparator on plasma MHD and shallow-water. FNO, ViT, and the BubbleML-modified U-Net remain; the UNetb label does not identify a new comparator.

E3.justification: The stated training rule changes from running sufficient epochs to imposing equal A100 budgets of 24 hours for plasma/Navier-Stokes and 48 hours for shallow-water. This is a reported protocol revision, without evidence establishing reruns. New evaluations measure coverage over the first 20 plasma and 10 shallow-water predictions and profile tokenizer variants at batch size 20. Existing splits and five-snapshot forecasting inputs remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds overlapping-tokenizer accuracy/cost ablations, a one-to-four-scale sensitivity study, computational tradeoff analysis, and quantitative uncertainty-calibration checks in Appendices B-D. These test previously unexamined component benefits and operating characteristics. The hierarchy/frequency-path ablation already existed in v1 Appendix B and is retained, including its numerical results.

E5.justification: v2 adds empirical coverage at nominal 90% and 95% confidence levels, including aggregate and variable-specific reporting in Tables 2, 10, and 11. The stated uncertainty band changes from 3σ in v1 Figure 4 to σ in v2 Figure 3. The existing 50 prediction samples per step and 100 stochastic trajectories are retained; additional independent training runs are not reported.

E6.justification: All 50 retained Table 1 values are identical; v2 adds ten DPOT entries rather than improving existing StFT scores. Substantial new results include tokenizer errors of 0.0986 without overlap versus 0.0307 with overlap on plasma, three/four-scale errors of 0.0385/0.0391, computational measurements, and coverage statistics. At nominal 90%, reported average coverage is 89.4% for plasma and 89.5% for shallow-water.

T1.justification: The autoregressive decomposition, rectified-flow interpolation and loss, scale-contribution measure, and Appendix A governing equations retain their mathematical substance. Explicit flow-time arguments and revised indices clarify the existing formulation. Neither version supplies new theorems or proofs relative to the other.

C1.justification: The principal architectural and forecasting contributions remain. v2 removes the introduction's specific 600%/20%/50% advantage claims and short-term-superiority wording, while strengthening the uncertainty contribution to explicitly claim empirically calibrated estimates. These refine the contribution claims without redefining the work.

C2.justification: v2 adds a regular-grid limitation concerning irregular geometries and explains temporarily higher StFT-F errors through distributional modeling and prediction variance. It also interprets the scale-count results as saturation and the coverage results as near-90% calibration. These are substantive but bounded additions to the retained interpretation of the method.

D1.justification: v2 adds DPOT hyperparameter ranges, explicit GPU-hour budgets, profiling batch size, and patch configurations for the scale sweep. Most existing implementation details remain. However, it omits v1 Appendix C's instruction to normalize residuals by their standard deviations; this is lost reproducibility information, not evidence that normalization was discontinued.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion concerning DPOT, P2C2Net, PDEBench, and plasma/probabilistic PDE research, while dropping the Kossaifi tensorized-FNO discussion. The central positioning against U-Net-style hierarchies and existing generative approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method explanations are extensively revised. Overlapping tokenization moves into the StFT-block explanation, experimental setup gains labeled subsections, and the results narrative is reorganized around ablations and additional analyses. Existing experimental-details and visualization appendices move from C/D to E/F.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main layout from two columns to one, merges the architecture diagrams into an expanded Figure 1, and adds a patch-subdivision illustration. It reorganizes existing plots and uncertainty panels, introduces logarithmic error axes, adds DPOT to visual comparisons, restructures ablation tables, and adds coverage and computational displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of central contributions: the previously unablated tokenizer is tested, scale selection is examined, a stronger DPOT comparator is included, and visual uncertainty evidence is supplemented with measured coverage. These address important evidential gaps in v1. The gains outweigh the omitted residual-normalization instruction and reporting inconsistencies, although calibration checks cover only early prediction windows and Figure 10's DPOT FLOPs disagree with Table 9, limiting the corresponding conclusions.
